title: How to reset your Windows password
body: If you forgot your Windows login password, press Ctrl+Alt+Delete, select 'Change a password' and follow the prompts. If you cannot sign in at all, contact IT to verify your identity before a manual reset is issued. Never share your password with anyone.

title: Reset your corporate email password
body: Visit the self-service portal at https://portal.helpdesk.local and choose 'Forgot password'. Enter your corporate email and follow the link sent to your recovery address or phone. The link expires after 15 minutes.

title: Set up the office VPN from home
body: Install the company VPN client from the software catalog, then use your normal corporate credentials. If you get error 721, disable IPv6 on the adapter and retry. Contact IT if the connection still fails after a reboot.

title: Troubleshooting slow or dropped WiFi
body: Move closer to an access point, forget and rejoin the network, and disable VPN before testing the speed. If the issue persists across devices, the access point may need a restart, so raise a ticket with the room and floor.

title: Connecting to the meeting room screens
body: To share to a meeting room screen, use the dongle in the room and select the room name from the list, or plug in with the HDMI cable for a wired connection. Press the reset button on the dongle if the screen is not listed.

title: Installing approved accounting software
body: All approved software is available in the internal app catalog. Request an install via the catalog which grants the required permissions automatically. Do not download accounting tools from external sites.

title: Printer setup and spooler restart
body: If a printer shows offline, restart the print spooler service on the print server. In the office you can also check the printer display for a paper jam or an 'offline' toggle on the front panel before opening a ticket.

title: Known email issues and workarounds
body: Outlook send failures are often caused by a full sent-items folder or an expired mailbox quota. Archive old mail, then restart Outlook. If you see 'operation failed', also try rebuilding the offline address book.

title: Reporting phishing emails
body: Report suspicious emails using the 'Report Phishing' button in Outlook or by forwarding the message as an attachment to phishing@helpdesk.local. Never click links or download attachments from unknown senders.

title: Recovering files from OneDrive
body: Deleted files can be recovered from the OneDrive recycle bin for 30 days. For older deletions, open a ticket for a restore from the nightly backup, which is kept for 90 days.

title: Setting up MFA on your phone
body: Download the authenticator app, scan the QR code shown in the security portal, and enter the six-digit code to activate it. Keep a backup method registered so you are never locked out.

title: Requesting hardware replacements
body: Hardware replacements are requested through the ticket system with the asset tag of the device. Depreciation policy requires devices to be at least three years old unless the failure blocks work.

title: Laptop battery health tips
body: Keep your laptop battery between 20% and 80%, enable battery saver, and avoid leaving it plugged in at 100% for long periods. Check the battery report with the battery-health tool in the helpdesk portal.

title: Docking station troubleshooting
body: If a docking station stops charging or detecting monitors, unplug the USB-C cable from both ends, wait 10 seconds, and reconnect. Update the dock firmware from the driver portal if the issue returns.

title: Screen flicker quick fixes
body: For a flickering monitor, check the display cable connection, lower the refresh rate to 60 Hz, and disable hardware acceleration in your browser. If it persists, the panel may need replacement.

title: Accessing shared network drives
body: Map the shared drive using the path provided on the intranet drive-mapping page. If you get 'access denied', your group membership may not cover the folder, so open a ticket with the folder name.

title: Managing mailbox permissions (managers)
body: Managers can grant shared mailbox and calendar permissions through the identity portal under 'Delegation'. Permission changes take effect within 10 minutes.

title: Booking meeting rooms
body: Meeting rooms are booked through the room-booking portal. Select the room, date and time, then confirm. Rooms with AV equipment are marked with a projector icon.

title: Software license requests
body: License requests are submitted via the app catalog and approved by the line manager. Licenses are allocated within two business days and appear under 'My licenses'.

title: Antivirus exceptions for internal tools
body: Internal tools signed by our certificate can be added to the antivirus exception list. Open a ticket with the file hash and the tool name; exceptions are reviewed weekly for safety.

title: Restoring files from backup
body: Self-service restore covers the last 30 days from the backup portal. Older data is restored on request and can take up to 48 hours depending on the volume size.

title: VPN error 721 troubleshooting
body: Error 721 indicates a protocol negotiation failure. Disable IPv6, delete the VPN profile and recreate it, then connect again. If it persists, check the security portal for an expired certificate.

title: Clear browser cache for web apps
body: Many web app failures are fixed by clearing the browser cache. Use Ctrl+Shift+Delete, choose 'cached images and files' and reload the page. Hard reload with Ctrl+Shift+R is a quick first step.

title: Set up email on a new phone
body: Use the company mobile management portal to configure the corporate mailbox automatically. You must be enrolled in the mobile device management profile first.

title: Remote desktop access guide
body: Remote Desktop is available through the remote access gateway at https://rdg.helpdesk.local. You must be on the VPN and use the same account you log in to your machine with.

title: Security awareness: password hygiene
body: Use a passphrase of at least 12 characters, do not reuse passwords across services, and enable multi-factor authentication everywhere it is offered. Report suspected compromise immediately.

title: Decommissioning old accounts (offboarding)
body: When an employee leaves, the manager initiates offboarding in the identity portal. Accounts are disabled within an hour and data is archived for 90 days before deletion.

title: New employee IT onboarding checklist
body: New hires receive their laptop, badge and mailbox credentials on day one. The onboarding ticket covers software licenses, the VPN profile and a security awareness training assignment.

title: Troubleshooting Outlook send failures
body: When sending fails, first check your mailbox quota, then restart Outlook in safe mode. Verify the recipient's address is not on your blocked list and that the mail server shows healthy status.

title: Excel performance tips
body: For large workbooks, disable automatic calculation, use structured tables, and remove volatile functions like INDIRECT. Saving as binary .xlsb format also reduces file size and open time.

title: Teams audio and video troubleshooting
body: If the microphone or camera is not detected in Teams, check the device permissions in the operating system, select the correct device under Teams settings, and restart the Teams app.

title: Network drive mapping on Windows
body: Map drives with 'net use' using the standard drive letters listed on the intranet page. Drive mappings persist across reboots only when you select 'reconnect at sign-in'.

title: VLAN port activation request
body: New switch ports are activated by raising a network request with the room, the wall socket number and the purpose of the connection. Activation normally completes within one business day.

title: Webcam not detected fixes
body: If the built-in webcam is not detected, reinstall the camera driver from the driver portal and check that the camera is not disabled in the device manager and in the privacy settings.

title: External drive not recognized fixes
body: Try the drive on another USB port, then another machine. Check the disk manager for an unallocated volume. If the drive spins up but never appears, it may need a data recovery evaluation.

title: Data loss incident reporting
body: Report any suspected data loss immediately with the affected folder path and the last known good timestamp. Preserve the system state and do not write new data to the affected volume.

title: Phishing red flags checklist
body: Watch for urgent language, mismatched sender domains, unexpected attachments and links that differ from the displayed address. When in doubt, report the message instead of clicking.

title: Password expiry and self-service reset
body: Passwords expire every 90 days. You can change them in advance from the security portal without waiting for the expiry reminder.

title: MFA device replacement
body: If you get a new phone, re-register your authenticator app in the security portal and remove the old device. Keep a second method such as a backup code list active while you migrate.

title: Service outage status page access
body: Live service status and scheduled maintenance are published on the status page at https://status.helpdesk.local. Outages affecting the office are also announced on the internal chat channel.

title: Installing a network printer manually
body: If a printer is missing from your device list, add it by IP address using the printer's panel to read the address, then install the matching driver from the driver portal. Ask your floor's printer champion if the model is unknown.

title: Printer paper jam recovery
body: Open the front and rear panels of the printer and pull the paper out slowly in the direction it was feeding. Check the fuser area for torn pieces, close the panels and press the resume button. Reopen the panels if the jam message stays.

title: Printing in color for the design team
body: Color printing is available on the design-floor printers. In the print dialog choose the color printer from the list; standard floor printers are black and white only.

title: Toner and ink ordering
body: Toner is restocked automatically by the facilities team when the printer reports low. If a printer is out of toner and not replaced within a day, raise a ticket with the room number.

title: Scan-to-email setup
body: Use the scan-to-email feature on the printer touchscreen by selecting the 'Email' destination and typing the recipient address. Files are sent as PDF unless you choose JPEG. The address book stores frequent recipients.

title: VPN slow performance fixes
body: Slow VPN speeds are often caused by bandwidth-heavy apps. Close video calls and large transfers before testing, and connect to the closest VPN region listed in the client. If speed stays low, check your home network's upload capacity.

title: VPN login loop: certificate not valid
body: If the VPN client loops at 'certificate not valid', the certificate on the gateway may have been renewed. Delete the saved profile and re-import the new one from the download portal, then log in again.

title: VPN on personal devices policy
body: Personal devices can use the VPN for web access only, with the personal-device profile. Company data must stay on managed machines; the personal profile has no access to internal file shares.

title: VPN DNS leak check
body: After connecting, verify your traffic is routed through the office by checking the public IP on the VPN status page. If the IP still shows your home location, flush the DNS cache and reconnect.

title: Unlock a locked Windows account
body: If your Windows account is locked after failed attempts, wait 15 minutes or use the self-service unlock on the portal. For repeated locks, reset the password and check for scheduled tasks running with your credentials.

title: Changing your password on a domain computer
body: Press Ctrl+Alt+Delete and choose 'Change a password'. Enter the current password once and the new one twice. Passwords must be at least 12 characters and cannot repeat the last five passwords.

title: Password manager onboarding
body: The approved password manager is available in the app catalog. On first launch, import the shared company vault entry and enable the browser extension for autofill. Keep the master password offline and never share it.

title: Single sign-on setup
body: Most web applications use single sign-on. Open the app, choose 'Sign in with company account' and you will be redirected to the corporate login. If a legacy app asks for a separate password, request SSO enablement for it.

title: Outlook PST archive for mailbox cleanup
body: Archive old mail locally with AutoArchive into a PST file to free mailbox space. The archive file is stored on your OneDrive and travels with you. Folders must be re-enabled for archiving in the folder settings.

title: Set an out-of-office in Outlook
body: Open Outlook, choose File, then Automatic Replies. Enable 'Send automatic replies' and type the message for colleagues and another for external senders. Set the time range if you know when you will be back.

title: Shared calendar permissions
body: Share your calendar from the calendar settings under 'Sharing and permissions'. Managers can grant full-delegation access through the identity portal. Delegate calendars show in the same folder tree after a restart.

title: Email forwarding rules
body: Create forwarding rules under Outlook rules or the web mail settings. Rules can forward to your personal mailbox only when approved for that purpose. Onward forwarding is logged for security review.

title: Mailbox size limits explained
body: Mailboxes have a 50 GB quota. Near the limit you will see warnings and sending stops at 49 GB. Use archiving or delete large attachments before requesting a quota exception.

title: Access point coverage map
body: The access point coverage map is available on the network portal. Green areas have strong signal, yellow are weaker. If your desk is yellow, check with IT about an additional access point for your area.

title: Guest WiFi access
body: Visitors use the Guest network and a code from the reception desk. The guest code rotates daily and limits speed to 10 Mbps. No internal resources are reachable from the guest network.

title: Ethernet speed troubleshooting
body: Wired connections should negotiate 1 Gbps. Check the link speed in the network settings; if it shows 100 Mbps, the cable or port may be faulty. Swap the cable and test another port before requesting a port inspection.

title: Firewall port request process
body: Requests to open firewall ports go through the security team with a business justification and an expiry date. Open ports are reviewed quarterly and removed when no longer justified.

title: DNS issues on client machines
body: If a site resolves to the wrong address or fails, flush the DNS cache with 'ipconfig /flushdns' and check the configured DNS servers point to the internal resolvers. Persistent issues are logged with the affected domain.

title: Internet outage announcement channels
body: When the internet is down, the status page and the internal chat channel carry announcements. IT updates the status page every 15 minutes during outages. Avoid opening duplicate tickets while a known outage is in progress.

title: Ordering a second monitor
body: Request an additional monitor through the hardware request form with your desk number. Two monitors are standard for most roles; a third requires manager approval. Delivery takes about a week.

title: Peripherals warranty info
body: Mice, keyboards, headsets and monitors carry a three-year warranty from issue. Failed peripherals are replaced at the IT desk with the asset tag. Battery-powered accessories are covered only for the first year.

title: Cleaning your devices safely
body: Power off devices and use a lint-free cloth slightly dampened with isopropyl alcohol. Never spray liquid directly on a device, and avoid compressed air blowing into vents from close range, which can damage fans.

title: Laptop delivery timeline for new hires
body: New-hire laptops are prepared within three business days of the start notice and delivered on day one. Delays happen when the onboarding request is incomplete, so confirm the manager submitted the request first.

title: Device swap before travel
body: Before international travel, request a device swap to a travel laptop with the correct power adapters and preloaded VPN. Travel devices are issued at least a week before departure and returned on arrival.

title: Headsets supported list
body: The supported headset list contains models with verified microphone and speaker quality in Teams. Wireless headsets pair through the dongle included in the box. Unlisted headsets may have driver issues and are not supported.

title: Phone charging port issues
body: If the phone charging port is loose or slow, try a different cable first, then a different charger. Ports clogged with lint can be cleaned carefully with a wooden toothpick. Replacements are handled under the phone warranty.

title: Updating software safely
body: Apply operating system and security updates within a week of release. Business applications receive updates through the catalog which stages them for the maintenance window. Never disable updates to work around a problem.

title: Uninstalling programs on a company laptop
body: Software removal on company laptops is done through the catalog to keep the device inventory accurate. If you need a program removed immediately, request it in a ticket and the removal is scheduled.

title: Browser support policy
body: The supported browsers are Chrome and Edge on the current release plus the previous one. Web applications are tested against both. Safari is usable for web mail only on unmanaged devices.

title: Teams meeting recording
body: Record meetings from the meeting controls with 'Record and transcribe'. Recordings are stored in OneDrive and shared with participants automatically. Recordings are kept for 180 days then deleted.

title: Excel VBA macros policy
body: Macros must be signed by the company certificate to run. Unsigned macros are blocked by default. Request signing through the developer portal and test in the sandbox first.

title: PDF signing workflow
body: Sign PDFs with the company signing tool which applies the certificate-based signature. Digital signatures are legally binding; never paste a scanned image of a signature onto official documents.

title: Installing Python on dev machines
body: Developers install Python from the catalog which sets up the managed version and environment variables. Use the pinned project version listed in each repository's readme rather than upgrading globally.

title: Docker Desktop setup
body: Docker Desktop is available from the catalog for developers. Enable the WSL 2 backend and allocate at least 8 GB of memory in settings. VPN users must allow the Docker subnet through the split tunnel.

title: Version control client guide
body: The standard client is configured with your company credentials from the developer portal. Clone repositories over HTTPS and set your identity to the corporate email. Push and pull require your VPN connection from home.

title: IDE license activation
body: IDE licenses are bound to your corporate account. Activate through the IDE login with your company credentials; the license server validates automatically. Licenses are released when you change roles.

title: Role-based access request form
body: System access is requested through the access form which lists each system and role. Requests are approved by the system owner and the line manager. Most access is granted within one business day.

title: Temporary access for contractors
body: Contractor access is created by the engaging manager with a start and end date. The account is disabled automatically on the end date. Extensions must be approved before the current access expires.

title: Shared mailbox access guide
body: Access to shared mailboxes is granted through the identity portal by the mailbox owner. You can then open the mailbox in Outlook from the folder pane. Sensitive mailboxes require an additional approval.

title: Unlocking badge access
body: Badge access is tied to your badge ID and the zones assigned by your manager. If a door does not open, check the badge portal to confirm the zone is active and report the door and badge ID if it should be.

title: Data classification levels
body: Data is classified as public, internal, confidential or restricted. Confidential and restricted data stays on approved storage and is never placed on personal devices or public sharing links.

title: Security incident reporting
body: Report suspected incidents immediately to the security mailbox with the time, systems involved and any observations. Do not delete evidence. The security team triages within one hour during business hours.

title: API key management
body: API keys are issued through the developer portal with scopes limited to the service needed. Keys are stored in the secrets vault, rotated every 90 days, and never committed to repositories.

title: Two-step verification backup codes
body: Generate backup codes from the security portal and store them offline. Each code works once. Regenerate the set whenever you suspect a code was exposed, so old codes stop working.

title: IT asset return process
body: Returning devices is arranged through the asset portal. Laptops and phones must have company data wiped first; the wipe is verified with a proof report. Devices are checked in at the IT desk with the asset tag.

title: Software procurement process
body: New software purchases start with a procurement request reviewed by security, licensing and the business owner. Trials are limited to 30 days. Approved software enters the catalog for distribution.

title: Reporting a lost badge
body: Report a lost badge immediately so the old one can be deactivated. Use the badge portal to mark it lost and order a replacement which takes two business days. The old badge stops working within the hour.

title: Moving desks: IT checklist
body: When moving desks, submit the move request with the new desk number. IT moves the phone, checks the network port and updates the asset location. Expect the move to complete within two business days.

title: Office equipment request
body: Office equipment such as chairs, monitor arms and footrests is ordered through the workplace request form. Ergonomic assessments are available through the health and safety team before large purchases.

title: Vendor software security review
body: Vendor software undergoes a security review before installation which covers data handling, patching and access controls. Reviews take up to two weeks, so plan early for vendor tools.

title: Printer queue stuck jobs
body: If a print job is stuck in the queue, cancel all jobs on the printer, restart the print spooler, and resubmit the document. Persistent stuck jobs indicate a corrupt driver, so reinstall the driver from the portal.

title: VPN split tunneling configuration
body: Split tunneling routes only office traffic through the VPN and keeps other traffic on your home connection. It is enabled by default on managed laptops. Disabling it is not supported because it breaks security policies.

title: WiFi 5GHz vs 2.4GHz guidance
body: The office WiFi broadcasts on both bands. 5 GHz gives higher speeds but shorter range; 2.4 GHz reaches farther. Devices connect to the best band automatically, but far desks may only see the 2.4 GHz network.

title: Laptop replacement eligibility
body: Laptops are replaced after four years or when the cost of repair exceeds a third of its value. Exceptions are made for hardware failures blocking work. Replacement requests need the asset tag and the failure description.

title: Monitor daisy-chaining
body: Monitors with a DisplayPort output can daisy-chain a second screen from a single laptop port. Both monitors must support the feature. If the second screen stays black, connect it directly to the dock instead.

title: Multifactor for finance applications
body: Finance applications require an additional multifactor step on top of SSO. Enroll the finance app in your authenticator app from the finance portal. Access is blocked until enrollment completes.

title: Password history policy
body: The system remembers the last five passwords and prevents reuse. Changing a password immediately back to an old one is also blocked for 24 hours. Complex passphrases avoid hitting the history rule often.

title: Mailbox delegation for assistants
body: Executives can delegate their mailbox to an assistant for reading and sending mail. The delegation is set in the identity portal by the executive. Delegates cannot delegate onward.

title: Conference room AV booking
body: Conference rooms with AV equipment are booked like normal rooms and marked with an AV icon. The AV setup is verified before the first booking of the day. Report broken equipment with the room name.

title: Software usage statistics
body: The software inventory reports usage per application per month. Managers can view usage for their teams to identify unused licenses for reclaim. Data is aggregated and anonymized in reports.

title: Email retention policy
body: Business email is retained for seven years from creation. Personal mail older than two years is archived automatically. Legal holds override automatic deletion and are applied by the compliance team.

title: Teams channel best practices
body: Use channels for topics instead of private chats to keep knowledge searchable. Name channels by team and topic, and archive channels when the work finishes. Video meetings in channels keep recordings in one place.

title: Searching the knowledge base
body: The knowledge base search covers titles and full article text. Use several short keywords instead of one long phrase. Articles are tagged by category and most common problem keywords.

title: New employee computer setup
body: New employees receive a fully configured laptop with the standard software image. The first login starts the setup wizard which installs the VPN, email and the password manager. Budget 30 minutes for first-time setup.

title: Home office equipment stipend
body: Remote staff can claim a home office stipend once a year for a desk, chair or monitor. The claim form requires receipts and manager approval. Equipment bought with the stipend remains the employee's property.

title: VPN for contractors
body: Contractors get a restricted VPN profile with access limited to the systems listed in their contract. The profile expires with the contract. Contractors cannot use the full employee VPN profile.

title: WiFi password change schedule
body: The internal WiFi password rotates every quarter and is announced on the intranet. The guest network code rotates daily. Connecting with the old password triggers a failed authentication message with the new hint.

title: Printer consumables delivery
body: Toner and paper are delivered to printer rooms on a weekly schedule. Deliveries happen on Wednesdays. Urgent requests are handled by the facilities team on the same day when a printer is completely out.

title: Access card zones
body: Badges are assigned to zones that match the employee's floor and office area. Zone changes are requested by the manager. Server rooms and the data center have separate restricted zones.

title: SSO troubleshooting
body: If single sign-on fails, confirm you are signed in to the corporate login first, then clear the application's cookies and retry. Error messages starting with AAD indicate an identity-side problem to report.

title: Office 365 suite issues
body: Office applications share one sign-in. If Word, Excel or Teams misbehaves after an update, run the Office repair tool from the app list. Corrupt profiles are fixed by the profile reset tool on the portal.

title: Antivirus scan scheduling
body: Antivirus full scans run nightly at 2 AM. On-demand scans are available from the tray icon. Exclusions are managed centrally and cannot be added locally.

title: Backup for personal folders
body: Desktop, Documents and Pictures are redirected to OneDrive automatically, which is backed up daily. Files stored elsewhere on the laptop are not backed up. Move important files into the redirected folders.

title: Badge tap troubleshooting
body: If the badge reader beeps red, hold the badge still for a second against the reader. Clean the badge chip with a dry cloth. Repeated failures across readers indicate the badge itself needs replacement.

title: Network cable certification
body: When a wall socket does not work, the network team certifies the cable run from the patch panel to the socket. Certification tests the eight wires, length and signal quality. A certified cable shows green link on both ends. If the test fails, the socket is scheduled for re-termination, which takes a few hours. If the link is up but slow, run the speed test from the network portal to compare against the switch port speed. Faulty wall sockets are the most common cause of flaky office connectivity, so the certification is performed before any switch or client replacement is considered.

title: Keyboard layout switching
body: Switch the keyboard layout with the language bar or the shortcut set in the keyboard settings. The standard company layout is US English. Special layouts for other regions are available in the keyboard settings.

title: Mouse settings for left-handed users
body: Left-handed users can swap the mouse buttons in the mouse settings under 'primary button'. Pointer speed and acceleration are adjustable per user and stored in the profile.

title: Laptop camera privacy shutter
body: Company laptops have a physical privacy shutter on the camera. Slide it to cover the lens when not in a call. The shutter does not affect the microphone.

title: External webcam installation
body: Plug the external webcam into any USB port; the driver installs automatically. Select the external camera in the video app when it appears. A solid LED indicates the camera is active.

title: Headset echo cancellation
body: Echo on calls usually comes from loudspeakers. Use the headset for both audio and microphone in the app settings. Built-in echo cancellation works best when the microphone is close to the mouth.

title: Power adapter replacement
body: Power adapters are replaced under the laptop warranty or at cost after three years. The asset tag on the adapter matches the laptop. Charging problems should be tested with a known-good adapter first.

title: Battery calibration
body: If the battery percentage jumps around, calibrate it: charge to 100%, unplug and let it drain to 5%, then recharge fully. Calibration is rarely needed on modern batteries and is not a fix for short battery life.

title: RAM upgrade request
body: RAM upgrades are performed by IT for approved models. Check your current usage in the task manager before requesting. Upgrades beyond the standard configuration require a business justification.

title: SSD storage expansion
body: If the disk is full, first move files into OneDrive redirected folders and empty the recycle bin. Larger SSDs are installed for approved cases. Check the disk usage report in the hardware portal before requesting.

title: Thunderbolt port issues
body: Thunderbolt ports have a higher failure rate than other ports. Test peripherals on a different port first. Firmware updates for the dock resolve most Thunderbolt disconnects. Persistent issues get the dock replaced.

title: Smart card reader setup
body: The smart card reader driver installs from the catalog. Sign in with the card and PIN on supported machines. Card certificates expire yearly and are renewed by the security team.

title: Elevated privilege justification
body: Elevated privileges are granted for a defined period and a specific task. The request states the task, the systems and the end date. Privileges are reviewed monthly and removed when the task completes.

title: Data export approval
body: Exporting confidential data off approved storage requires approval from the data owner. Approved exports are logged with the destination. Unapproved exports are a security incident.

title: Guest network for vendors
body: Vendors use the guest network with the daily code. If a vendor needs access to a specific internal system, request a temporary contractor account instead of opening firewall access.

title: VoIP phone issues
body: VoIP phones show their status on the screen: green for registered, red for registration failure. Restart the phone by unplugging the network cable for ten seconds. If the phone stays red, check the switch port link and the phone's DHCP lease. Most registration failures are caused by port configuration or an expired certificate on the phone. One-way audio is usually a firewall or headset problem: test with the handset and then with the headset. If calls drop randomly, replace the network cable between the phone and the wall first, since a worn cable causes intermittent drops. Persistent issues are escalated to the voice team with the phone's MAC address printed on the label under the handset. When a phone was moved to a new desk, verify it received an IP from the correct VLAN, because phones moved across floors often pick up a lease from the wrong scope. Call quality complaints during peak hours should be checked against the switch port utilization graph, which the network team can pull on request. Always record the error code or the screen message before reporting, since the voice team triages most tickets by the message text.

title: VoIP softphone setup
body: The softphone app is installed from the catalog and signs in with your corporate credentials. Configure the headset as the audio device. Softphone calls over VPN have lower quality and are best made from the office network.

title: Video conference bandwidth
body: A video call uses about 4 Mbps in each direction. For stable calls, keep the office WiFi signal strong and avoid large downloads during the call. Conference rooms have dedicated bandwidth for video.

title: Wired vs wireless guidance
body: Wired connections are faster and more stable than WiFi. Desks with a network port should use wired for docking stations and daily work. WiFi is fine for meetings and light work.

title: Intranet site publishing
body: Internal sites are published by the web team through the intranet publishing process. The request includes the site name, content owner and target audience. Sites are reviewed for security before publishing.

title: Email spoofing report
body: If you receive mail that appears to come from a colleague but looks wrong, check the full sender address and report it as spoofing. The security team uses the report to add rules blocking the sender domain.

title: Application whitelisting
body: Applications on company machines run under a whitelist policy. Unlisted executables are blocked. To run a new tool, request whitelisting with the file hash and a business reason.

title: Software inventory
body: The software inventory lists every application installed on managed devices. Managers can pull a report for their team. Inventory data is refreshed nightly.

title: OS upgrade eligibility
body: Operating system upgrades are rolled out by department after compatibility testing. Eligibility is based on the department rollout schedule, not device age. Upgrades happen outside working hours.

title: Test environment access
body: Test environments are accessed with test accounts that differ from production. Test credentials are shared through the environment portal and rotated monthly. Test data is never production data.

title: Production data access rules
body: Production data access is logged and monitored. Read access is granted per system on request. Write access requires a change ticket and is limited in time.

title: Business continuity drills
body: The company runs continuity drills twice a year, announced a week ahead. During a drill, some systems are unavailable for a few hours. Feedback from drills updates the continuity plans.

title: Disaster recovery plan
body: The disaster recovery plan covers restoring core systems within four hours of a major outage. Backup systems are tested quarterly. The plan is documented in the operations portal.

title: IT service catalog
body: The IT service catalog lists every service with its request form, target response time and owner. Start with the catalog for any IT need. Services not listed are requested through a general ticket.

title: Self-service password reset kiosk
body: The password reset kiosk in the lobby lets you reset a forgotten password after identity verification with your badge and a code to your registered phone. The kiosk resets the domain password, email password and unlocks the account in one step. After the reset, log in to your machine with the new password within the hour. The kiosk does not reset the VPN PIN; that is done from the security portal. If your phone is not registered, visit the IT desk with your badge and a second form of ID. The kiosk is available 24/7 and prints a confirmation slip for your records. Repeated resets on the same account trigger a review by the security team to rule out compromise.

title: Kiosk login procedures
body: Kiosks in the lobby and the cafeteria accept badge tap or manual login. Badge tap grants the default kiosk profile. Manual login requires the full corporate credentials and signs you out after 30 minutes of inactivity.
